/-!
# Erdős Problem 328

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/328](https://www.erdosproblems.com/328)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*.
  Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial
  number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980).
- [Er80e] Erdős, P., *Some applications of Ramsey's theorem to additive number theory*.
  European J. Combin. (1980), 43-46.
- [NeRo85] J. Nešetřil and V. Rödl, *Two proofs in combinatorial number theory*.
  Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1985), 185-188.
-/

@[expose] public section

open AdditiveCombinatorics

namespace Erdos328

/--
Suppose $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ and $C>0$ is such that $1_A\ast 1_A(n)\leq C$ for all
$n\in\mathbb{N}$. Can $A$ be partitioned into $t$ many subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_t$ (where
$t=t(C)$ depends only on $C$) such that $1_{A_i}\ast 1_{A_i}(n)<C$ for all $1\leq i\leq t$
and $n\in \mathbb{N}$?

The answer is no. Asked by Erdős and Newman. Nešetřil and Rödl [NeRo85] have shown the
answer is no for all $C$ (even if $t$ is also allowed to depend on $A$).

Erdős [Er80e] had previously shown the answer is no for $C=3,4$ and infinitely many other
values of $C$.

See also [774].

The linked proof writes the representation function as
`Set.ncard {p : ℕ × ℕ | p.1 ∈ A ∧ p.2 ∈ A ∧ p.1 + p.2 = n}`, which counts the same ordered
pairs as `sumRep`, and states the partition condition as a named definition with the same two
conjuncts used below. Its `∃ t` additionally carries `1 ≤ t`, which costs nothing: `t = 0`
forces `A = ∅`, and `A = {1}` has all representation counts at most `C` for `C ≥ 1`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Jayyhk/erdos-lean/blob/f8a51976fd2e66a52b4928c109fb9ae877a1a507/problems/328/Erdos328.lean"]
theorem erdos_328 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ C : ℕ, 0 < C →
      ∃ t : ℕ, ∀ A : Set ℕ, (∀ n, sumRep A n ≤ C) →
        ∃ P : Fin t → Set ℕ, (⋃ i, P i) = A ∧
          Set.univ.PairwiseDisjoint P ∧
          ∀ i, ∀ n, sumRep (P i) n < C := by
  sorry

end Erdos328

reformulations.difference: Lean restricts C to positive natural numbers, whereas the source simply says C > 0, which could also allow positive real constants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Representation counts are integers. At an integer threshold, the real-valued and natural-valued inequalities agree. At a noninteger threshold C, every integer count ≤ C is already < C, so the one-cell partition works. Thus allowing all positive real thresholds gives exactly the same universal question. Proved as Review328.natural_vs_real_C in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The cited formal proof uses Set.ncard of the ordered representation set, a named partition predicate, an explicit 1 ≤ t, and a negation rather than False ↔. The reviewed statement uses sumRep, inline partition conditions, and unrestricted t : ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each n, the representation set is finite and equals the filtered antidiagonal counted by sumRep. The named partition predicate has exactly the same union and disjointness conditions. A uniform witness t cannot be zero: for C ≥ 1, A = {1} satisfies the representation bound, but a Fin 0-indexed union cannot cover it. Finally, False ↔ P is equivalent to ¬P. Proved the complete equivalence as Review328.equivalent_to_cited_proof in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes: Checked the sole declaration, including quantifier dependencies, partition semantics, empty sets, t = 0, C = 1, and representation-count finiteness. The cited proof compiles successfully and its reported axioms contain no sorryAx. The exact reviewed statement also has an independent elementary proof using C = 1 and A = {1}; this boundary case is already admitted by the webpage's explicit wording, so it is not a Lean/source mismatch. The theorem records failure of the global partition assertion, not the stronger parameter-by-parameter result mentioned in the prose. The older literature uses unordered representation counts, unlike the webpage's explicitly defined convolution, so that stronger historical result needs its own careful statement. Direct access to the Nešetřil–Rödl paper was blocked by AMS Cloudflare; its reported resolution is also recorded in the other primary references and the current problem page. Experiments and proofs are under /workspace/review/; the reviewed file was not modified.
